@krwq The relationship between this issue/PR and #73687 was unclear to me. I'm going to go ahead and move this issue to 8.0.0, but here's what I recommend:

1. If #67198 gets merged in before the .NET 7 RC 1 snap on Monday, that will be nice! We can change this issue milestone back to 7.0.0.
2. If not, but it gets merged in next week, we can consider requesting for it to be ported into the RC1 branch (and announce it as a breaking change if necessary).
3. Otherwise, it will be part of .NET 8; I wouldn't want to introduce it in RC2.
8.0.0 is fine. The issue I fixed was found while adding annotations to S.S.C.Xml and made it confusing to annote that's the only relationship

review_comments: seems to me that wither `DeformatterAlgorithm` or `CreateFromName` is badly annotated or we're missing checks somewhere here

`DeformatterAlgorithm` looks correct - it has a public setter that doesn't check for the value being assinged.

`CreateFromName` also **can** return null.
is it actually possible for this to return null? we seem to be throwing when user tries to add null
It doesn't look like it, but it must match the index operator for `IList`

I don't expect this to be fixed, just unresolving as FYI:
for return values you can make it non-nullable even if interface returns nullable (for setter it has to match but you can make it non-nullable with `[AllowNull]`)
It doesn't really matter for explicit interface implementations; no one ever sees these annotations (other than someone looking for them via reflection).
I assume the `?` is here because of the interface implementation? the getters can still be non-null though because that doesn't break interface
Yes, it's to satisfy the interface. `Item` is already non-null.
This doesn't look right.  The setter is explicitly throwing an exception if value is null.  Same for CipherValue below.
Yes, I missed the fact that the constructors call either one of two setters, each of which guarantee non-null.
Actually, there is a default constructor too. I could be wrong, but I think these **do** need to be nullable...

Making them nullable implies you can set them to null, but the setter explicitly throws for null.  If it's going to remain `public CipherReference? CipherReference`, then it also needs `[DisallowNull]`.

But somebody _could_ do `new CipherData().CipherReference.ToString()` and get an NRE.  That would be pretty silly though, so could you clarify if we should be annotating for every concievable usage, or just for 'reasonable' usage. (or perhaps I've missed something completely...?)

We're talking past each other. It should be:
```C#
[DisallowNull]
public CipherReference? CipherReference
```
which says the property may return null but can't be set to null.
I see. Thank you.
[DisallowNull]
nit: that seems like rather weird annotation to have on the setter, I'd recommend avoiding it (feel free to ignore this assuming it doesn't flow to the ref)
I'm pretty sure this was the result of other PR feedback. I've lost the history because of all the rebases required because of the age of this PR.

I can't comment on it directly, but Recipient above also appears like it would benefit from an [AllowNull].  In general, if the setter allows a null to be set and the getter checks for null and returns non-null, the property can be non-nullable with [AllowNull].

since you annotated constructor as non-nullable I'd expect this to be non-null and all related members, or alternatively ctor to accept null but looking at the existing setter I'd assume this is just missing null check in the ctor
It's nullable as there are multiple constructors, not all of which set it.

Is `null` ever gets added into this list? If no, it makes sense to assume it cannot contain `null`s, and annotate is accordingly (since this collection is internal). This will help reduce the number of `!`s in code that uses it

Unfortunately, this and other methods are implementations of `IList`:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/263416/161136589-09a42be0-4484-4ce2-be67-4600b2932f90.png)

I don't know if there's a standard way that is resolved in these types of PRs?
Oh, it implements `IList`. Missed that. Than there's no way around it I suppose..
is this actually nullable if we throw when null is added?
same comment for every IList
As far as I know, it needs to match the `IList` signature.
CanonicalizationMethod below is another example of a property that should be [AllowNull]

```suggestion
        [MemberNotNull(nameof(_containingDocument))]
        [MemberNotNull(nameof(m_signature))]
        [MemberNotNull(nameof(_safeCanonicalizationMethods))]
        private void Initialize(XmlElement? element)
```

And then `m_signature` (and others) can be marked as non-nullable, and `!`s can be removed.
A lot of files in this PR don't look related, and have merge conflicts.  Presumably there's a misplaced commit in here somewhere.
Ah, yes. I think what's happened is that I looked at nullability 'solution wide'. I'll revert these ones

I've reverted everything that is not directly related `System.Security.Cryptograph.Xml`. Sorry about that. I'm used to having solutions where everything in it is related and under the same folder as the solution.
double check this can be null given constructor annotation. if none of the code expects it might be worth filing an issue on ctor not throwing (same for CipherReference)
That one's easy: `byte[] ret = new CipherData().CipherValue;`, `ret` is `null`.
fair enough, I didn't notice parameterless ctor

I wonder if doing something like

```suggestion
        [return: NotNullIfNotNull("data")]
        internal static Stream? LogReferenceData(Reference reference, Stream? data)
```

will fix some unnecessary may-be-null states.

And since we'd NullReferenceException if `data` was null, maybe just getting rid of the `?`s here altogether is better.
Thank you!

I think it'd be better to fail with a cast exception rather than with a null reference exception in the event that attr is something other than the specified type.  So instead of using `!`, the foreach can be changed to be e.g.
```C#
foreach (CanonicalXmlAttribute attr in nsListToRender.GetKeyList())
```
and then just use `attr` in the loop, rather than the `as` cast and suppression.  Same for other cases above and below.

@stephentoub - yes, I think so too, however I didn't change it because I thought it would change the observable behaviour, which isn't encouraged in these types of PR (well, in general too, but _especially_ in these types of PRs).
@stephentoub - you may have missed the above comment; were my assumptions incorrect?
Thanks.  We can leave it for now and look at cleaning it up subsequently.
OK. Should I mark this as Resolved? Or should an Issue be created to track it?
